If (i) ξ(x; M(λ_i)) can be obtained from T_S by unstructured pruning using a mask m ∈ {0,1}^{|λ|}, (ii) after retraining the pruned network T_T the minimum-validation loss is reached in no more iterations than the dense source T_S (n_T ≤ n_S), and (iii) after retraining the pruned network T_T the validation accuracy is no worse than the dense source T_S (η_T ≥ η_S), then ξ(x; M(λ_i)) is regarded as a WLT-net (transferable winning lottery ticket) of T_S that retains the source task's representational capacity and therefore can serve as a sparse object for transfer learning from D_S to D_T.
